one_line: A Gandharan scribe-scholar bridging Greek and Kharosthi worlds in the early Buddhist manuscript culture.

appearance.age_look: mid-20s to early 30s, slim but sturdy from long hours of travel and writing
appearance.face: oval face with a straight nose, warm light-brown complexion typical of Gandhara, soft but alert brown eyes with thick brows, a faint ink-smudge scar on the right cheek, default expression gently focused and thoughtful as if mid-translation
appearance.hair: dark brown hair pulled into a neat topknot at the crown, sides and back smoothed and tied with a narrow red cloth band, a short well-kept beard and moustache framing the jaw, no turban or hat to keep the topknot visible
appearance.costume: a knee-length light-cream cotton tunic (kurta-like) with long sleeves and a simple round neck slit, worn over narrow dark-indigo woollen trousers; a soft dusty-ochre wool shawl draped over the left shoulder and wrapped once around the torso for warmth, its edge bordered with a subtle darker geometric band; a thin dark-brown leather belt at the waist from which a small pouch hangs; simple brown leather sandals with thong straps; minimal jewellery limited to a single small bronze ring on the left hand to mark modest status and practicality; textiles look slightly worn from travel but carefully maintained, reflecting the northwestern climate and Gandharan style
appearance.signature: a rolled birch-bark manuscript case slung diagonally across his back in a light-brown leather tube, plus in his right hand a slim reed stylus stained dark at the tip and a flat wooden writing board resting under his left arm, their surfaces showing faint lines of Kharosthi and Greek script

ref_desc: A light-brown Gandharan man with a neat dark-brown topknot, short beard, cream knee-length tunic, dark-indigo trousers, dusty-ochre shawl, brown leather belt and sandals, carrying a birch-bark manuscript tube, reed stylus and writing board in a palette of cream, ochre, indigo and brown.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of a Gandharan Kharosthi scribe: a light-brown man in his late twenties with an oval face, thoughtful brown eyes, a neat dark-brown topknot tied with a red band, and a short trimmed beard and moustache; dress him in a modest light-cream knee-length cotton tunic with long sleeves and a simple round neck slit, worn over narrow dark-indigo woollen trousers, with a dusty-ochre wool shawl draped over his left shoulder and wrapped once around his torso, its edge marked by a subtle darker geometric border; add a thin dark-brown leather belt at the waist with a small pouch, simple brown leather thong-strap sandals, and a single small bronze ring on his left hand; have a light-brown leather birch-bark manuscript tube slung diagonally across his back, and in his hands a slim dark-stained reed stylus and a flat wooden writing board etched faintly with Kharosthi and Greek characters; ensure the overall palette emphasises light cream, dusty ochre, dark indigo, brown leather and small deep-red accents, keeping his posture calm yet energetic as a bridge between scripts and cultures.
